applies_why: This judge text decides a link by the individual almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows and an open sign-sense, which is the link-weighing situation K-C governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'never verse by verse'—read as allowing underdetermination from open individual rows versus read as forbidding a link from being decided by isolated verse rows when the pressing witnesses are a chain.
why: The judge leaves D5 underdetermined because individual almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows are answered but the sign's sense remains open, which is verse-by-verse indecision rather than weighing the competing chains by footing as K-C requires.
